extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PIs), institutional sponsored programs staff, and NIH peer reviewers/SRG members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing how NIH Scientific Review Groups (study sections) conduct the first level peer review of grant applications, including reviewer roles, review criteria, scoring, confidentiality, and post-review communications. Intended to inform both applicants and reviewers about expectations and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: SRGs assess the overall impact that your proposed project (or resource, or training, or center, etc.) will likely have on the biomedical research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact scores reflect the reviewers’ overall assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. Reviewers give a preliminary Overall Impact score before the meeting; a final Overall Impact score for discussed applications is the mean of final impact scores from eligible members multiplied by 10, yielding a 10 (high impact) to 90 (low impact) scale. Preliminary scores may be used to determine which applications are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria (individual criterion scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign individual criterion scores for all scored review criteria; these scored criteria contribute to the Overall Impact score of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each reviewer uses their own judgement to determine how each criterion weighs into the Overall Impact score, unless specified differently in the funding opportunity. Criterion scores typically use a numerical scale of 1 to 9 but may also include non-numerical ratings. Assigned reviewers give separate scores for each review criterion before the SRG meeting; the individual scores of the assigned reviewers for these criteria are provided to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (required acceptability areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria that do not receive individual criterion scores but contribute to the Overall Impact score and in some cases must be acceptable before an award can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include protections for human subjects, vertebrate animals, and biohazards. Reviewers also make recommendations concerning protections for human subjects; inclusion of women, minorities, and children in clinical research; human embryonic stem cells; and other applicable areas. Some of these criteria need to be considered acceptable before NIH can award a grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations (non-scoring programmatic input)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations that do not receive individual criterion scores and do not contribute to the Overall Impact score but provide scientific expert input on programmatic issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: whether an application’s budget is sufficiently justified by the proposed project, or whether the project could be completed for a smaller budget (or in fewer years) than requested. These are used to inform programmatic decisions but do not affect scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH 9-point Scoring Scale and Calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most review criteria and overall impact are rated using a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) in whole numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the SRG meeting, each assigned reviewer gives a separate score for each review criterion and a preliminary Overall Impact score. For discussed applications, a final Overall Impact score is given by each eligible panelist; the mean of those final impact scores multiplied by 10 produces a 10–90 final Overall Impact score. Not Discussed (ND) applications (those unanimously judged less competitive) do not receive a numerical final Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned Reviewer Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers read each application thoroughly, write a critique summarizing the strengths and weaknesses, and assign a preliminary Overall Impact score and individual criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers receive access to applications approximately six weeks prior to the peer review meeting. At the meeting, the primary reviewer presents the application and starts the discussion; the other two assigned reviewers may provide additional comments. All assigned reviewers prepare written critiques (as directed by the SRO) and assign numerical scores to each scored review criterion. Their bulleted critiques (strengths and weaknesses) and criterion scores are included in the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the NIH extramural staff scientist designated federal official responsible for ensuring each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs assign at least three reviewers to each application; give all non-conflicted panel members access to applications; actively manage the peer review meeting to ensure fair and effective review and conflict management; prepare a resume of discussion for all applications to accurately reflect score-driving elements; and ensure compliance with review policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The chair serves as moderator of the discussion of scientific and technical merit of the applications under review and also serves as a peer reviewer for the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chair facilitates discussions during the meeting and helps ensure balanced, collegial discussion led by the SRO and meeting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria and qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are recruited based on scientific and technical qualifications and other considerations to ensure expertise appropriate for the applications under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include authority in their scientific field, dedication to high quality, fair, and objective reviews, ability to work collegially in a group setting, and balanced expertise appropriate for the applications under review. Reviewers are fully vetted for appropriate expertise, potential conflicts of interest, and other requirements based on NIH peer review policies. NIH provides reviewers extensive orientation and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest declaration and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest with specific applications following NIH guidance; conflicted reviewers are recused from discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the SRO opens the meeting, any reviewer with a conflict of interest is asked to leave the room before the group begins reviewing an individual application. The SRO documents and manages conflicts of interest. Federal officials who have a need-to-know may attend with advance approval from the SRO. Applicants may not contact reviewers to influence outcomes or try to access protected information; there are consequences for violating confidentiality or attempting to influence review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and integrity of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH review meetings are confidential; reviewers should not divulge information outside the meeting and must maintain confidentiality of peer review information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may not contact reviewers, send information directly to a reviewer, or try to access protected information related to the review. Reviewers receive orientation reminding them the meetings are confidential. Integrity and confidentiality policies are enforced and violations carry consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement contents and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After the meeting, all reviewed applications receive an impact score and a summary statement prepared by the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH typically releases scores in eRA Commons within 3 business days and uploads the summary statement within about 30 days. The summary statement includes Impact Score and Percentile (if applicable), a brief summary of the SRG discussion (written by the SRO), criterion scores from the assigned reviewers, bulleted critiques (strengths and weaknesses) from the assigned reviewer, budget recommendations, and any administrative comments. Many summary statements also include a percentile comparing the application's impact score relative to other applications reviewed by that committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Discussed (ND) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications unanimously judged by the SRG to be less competitive (typically rank in the bottom half) are not discussed at the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Discussed applications do not receive a numerical final Overall Impact score. Preliminary scoring and triage practices may be used to determine which applications are discussed in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH's peer review appeal system allows investigators and applicant organizations to seek reconsideration of the initial review results if they believe the review process was flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid grounds for appeal include bias of a reviewer, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the review outcome. The policy does not apply to appeals of NIH funding decisions, appeals concerning extensions of MERIT awards, or appeals of the technical evaluation of R&D contract projects through the NIH peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and study section suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may suggest study section assignments when submitting their application using the PHS Assignment Request Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CSR Assisted Referral Tool (ART) can help identify CSR study sections that might be appropriate for review. Assignments consider applicant requests but the primary determinants are the published study section guidelines and CSR policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of reviewer outputs that affect applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer outputs provided to applicants include individual criterion scores, preliminary and final impact scores, bulleted critiques, and any budget recommendations or administrative comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outputs appear in the summary statement and are released via eRA Commons. Applicants should contact the NIH Program Official after receiving the summary statement to discuss fundability and next steps.
